definitions: A fair-weather friend, partner, or associate who disappears when things are difficult and reappears when circumstances improve.
Also: to resurface or pop back up after being absent during hard times — 'lulutang siya kapag maganda na ang sitwasyon.'
etymology: From Tagalog 'lutang' (to float; rising to the surface). 'Lulutang' is the future tense: 'will float up/resurface'. Metaphor: like a piece of debris that sinks during a storm and floats back up when calm returns. Distinct from 'lutang' (spaced out/disconnected, from Shanti Dope file).

examples.text: Lulutang siya kapag okay na ulit — ganoon lang siya
examples.source: Flow G x Skusta Clee x Yuridope, Gaga (viral 2024)

examples.text: Lulutang na naman siya ngayon na sikat ka na

regional_notes: Note: 'lutang' has two related but distinct meanings in youth slang — fair-weather behavior ('lulutang') and spacey/not paying attention ('lutang ka').

definitions: Secretly or subtly; qualifying an admission as something understated or not widely advertised.
Used to soften a statement: 'low key gusto ko siya' = I secretly/kind of like them.
Something done without fanfare or publicity: 'low key lang ang selebrasyon namin'.
etymology: Borrowed directly from English Gen Z slang 'low key' (secretly, quietly, modestly). Fully integrated into Filipino Taglish speech and rap lyrics — appearing naturally alongside Tagalog words without adaptation.

definitions: 'Forget you' — a defiant breakup proclamation and declaration of moving on.
Functions as a cultural meme and empowerment phrase used on social media to announce closure from a person or situation.
etymology: Standard Tagalog: 'kalimutan' (to forget) + 'ka' (you). While grammatically standard, the specific phrase has evolved into a cultural touchstone for Filipino youth breakup culture in 2025, driven by Skusta Clee's Billboard chart hit.

definitions: 'Give it a rest / stop / enough of this' — telling someone or a situation to cease; going beyond the literal meaning of 'rest'.
Used to tell someone to stop causing trouble, stop arguing, or give up on a lost cause.
etymology: Standard Tagalog 'pahinga' (rest/take a break; imperative 'pahinga' = rest now) + 'na' (already/now/intensifier). In youth slang, 'pahinga na' evolved beyond literal rest to mean 'knock it off / you're done / give it a rest'.

definitions: Gossip; rumors; the act of spreading or consuming gossip about others.
Can be used as a noun ('anong chismis?') or culturally to describe a nosy, gossiping person or atmosphere.
etymology: From Spanish 'chismes' (gossip/rumors). Deep-rooted in Filipino culture for centuries. The personified form is 'Marites' (a gossipy character archetype). The slang is reinforced by a 2024 collaborative rap track titled 'Chismis' by multiple OPM artists.

examples.text: Anong chismis? — May bago bang issue?
